Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelTcpPort_too: TCP port on which the server accepts players whose network drops UDP. They choose TCP under "Tunnel" in their server entry and enter this port. 0 turns the tunnel off. Open this TCP port in the firewall. Takes effect when the server starts.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpPort_too: UDP port on which the server accepts players whose network loses packets. They choose KCP under "Tunnel" in their server entry and enter this port. 0 turns the KCP tunnel off. Open this UDP port in the firewall. Takes effect when the server starts; the KCP settings below go to each player when they join.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpInterval: How often the KCP tunnel checks for acknowledgements and resends. Lower reacts faster to loss and uses a little more CPU. Recommended: 10.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpResend_t: Resend a packet as soon as this many later packets were acknowledged before it, without waiting for its timeout. 0 turns fast resend off. Recommended: 2.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpNoConges: On: the KCP tunnel does not slow down when packets are lost, which is what keeps it fast on a lossy network. Off: it backs off like TCP, which can help a link that is simply too slow for the game. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpWindow_t: How many packets may be on the way unacknowledged, each direction. Too small stalls map downloads on a distant server. Recommended: 1024.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelKcpMtu_tool: Largest UDP packet the KCP tunnel sends. Lower it if players on some networks connect but stall. Recommended: 1350.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelFecDataShar: The KCP tunnel adds repair packets for each group of this many packets. Recommended: 10.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelFecParitySh: Repair packets sent with each group: up to this many lost packets of a group are rebuilt at once, without waiting for a resend. 0 turns FEC off. On a quiet connection most groups are small, so FEC can roughly double the bandwidth. Recommended: 3.
Sandbox_Dont39AllInOne_TunnelFecFlushMil: Longest wait before a group that is not full gets its repair packets, so packets sent slowly are protected too. Lower recovers sooner and sends more repair packets. Recommended: 20.
